correctness.rationale: The exact matrix formula for \(CD_dC\) is \(n^{-1}\sum_{j=k}^n d_j/j\) below the diagonal; mean-zero periodicity yields its \(O((nk)^{-1})\) entry bound and a convergent Hilbert–Schmidt square sum. The Gram kernel \(\sum_{n\ge\max(j,k)}e_n/n^2\) is \(O(\max(j,k)^{-2})\) and Hilbert–Schmidt. These give quotient identities \(aba=ma^2\) and \(a^*b^*ba=\mu a^*a\). The Cesàro image \(a\) is normal by explicit compact selfcommutator, and its norm is exactly \(2\) by Hardy and weakly null extremizing packets. Consequently \(\|(ba)^p\|=2^p\sqrt\mu|m|^{p-1}\); the spectral radius and nonzero square-zero special case follow. The published source date, coefficient normalizations, complex conjugations and the zero-mean first-power boundary were independently checked. The supplied exact-rational finite checker passed 2,884 diagnostics, with finite tests not used to certify infinite results.

value.rationale: The object is a natural signed/complex periodic extension of the classical Rhaly/Cesàro operator. The exact all-power essential norm distinguishes the first coefficient mean from mean squared modulus and yields the precise essential spectral radius. At mean zero it gives the structurally striking nonzero square-zero Calkin element, with square Hilbert–Schmidt and positive essential norm; the alternating modulation has exactly the same Gram operator as ordinary Cesàro while changing essential spectral radius from \(2\) to \(0\). This is an intrinsic operator-theoretic separation that is not a small numerical improvement or a routine normalization.
